newsitem.title: USA: American Standard rejects Tyco offer.
newsitem.headline: American Standard rejects Tyco offer.

text.p: American Standard Companies Inc. said Monday it rejected a merger proposal from Tyco International Ltd., which a published report said was worth about $4 billion.

American Standard, which manufactures plumbing supplies, air conditioners and car brakes, confirmed that it received a proposal from Tyco more than a month ago and its board had decided not to pursue the matter.
The company did not reveal any details of the proposal, but the Wall Street Journal said Monday that it had obtained a copy of the Tyco offer, which amounted to $50 a share, or about $4 billion.
A spokesman for Tyco declined to comment on the report.

The reported offer would mean that Tyco, a diversified manufacturing company, would be paying a steep premium for American Standard, whose shares closed Friday at $40.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Neither American Standard nor Tyco began trading when the NYSE opened Monday morning. Tyco lost 50 cents to $54.125 when it opened just before noon.

"American Standard's board of directors reviewed the proposal and concluded that strategies already in place are working and the best way to increase earnings and shareholder value is to stay focused on carrying out the strategies as an independent company," the company said in a statement.
"Accordingly, the company declined any interest in that proposal, has not had any discussions with Tyco concerning it and no discussions are contemplated."

American Standard noted in its statement that its stock price had doubled since it went public in February 1995 and it plans to proceed with an announced secondary public offering and repurchase of shares next month.

American Standard, based in Piscataway, N.J., is the parent of companies that produce Trane and American Standard air conditioning products, American Standard, Ideal Standard, and Standard plumbing products and WABCO commercial and utility vehicle brake and control systems.
Tyco, based in Exeter, N.H., made a number of acquisitions last year but still has a strong cash flow, analysts said.
